thread.title: ETF Preview: ETFs, Futures Positive Ahead of Open as Apple Leads Tech Sector Higher

author: MT Newswires
title: ETF Preview: ETFs, Futures Positive Ahead of Open as Apple Leads Tech Sector Higher
text:
Shutterstock photo Active broad-market exchange-traded funds ahead of Tuesday's regular session:
SPDR Select Sector Fund - Financial ( XLF ): -0.3%
SPDR S&P 500 ( SPY ): +0.1%
iShares MSCI Emerging Index Fund ( EEM ): -0.3%
iShares Inc iShares MSCI Brazil ETF ( EWZ ): -1.4%
VelocityShares Daily 2x VIX Short Term ETN ( TVIX ): +1.3%
Broad Market Indicators
Broad-market exchange-traded funds, including SPY, IWM and IVV were higher. Actively traded PowerShares QQQ (QQQ) was up 0.2%.
US stock futures were in positive territory ahead of the open, led by gains in the tech sector. Apple (AAPL) shares were higher after the company presented "critical" changes aimed to strengthen its ecosystem in the Worldwide Developers Conference.
In economic data news, the Markit services purchasing managers index for May will be released at 9:45 a.m. ET, followed by the ISM's services index for May and job openings for April at 10 am ET.
Power Play: Consumer
Consumer Staples Select Sector SPDR (XLP) and other funds Vanguard Consumer Staples ETF (VDC) and iShares Dow Jones US Consumer Goods (IYK) were flat.
Consumer Discretionary Select Sector SPDR (XLY) and retail funds SPDR S&P Retail (XRT), PowerShares Dynamic Retail (PMR) and Market Vectors Retail ETF (RTH) were inactive in pre-market territory.
Francesca's (FRAN) rose 1% after it reported fiscal Q4 earnings above Street views while meeting sales expectations for the quarter. The company reported adjusted EPS of $0.20 for quarter ended Feb. 3, down from $0.39 a year ago, but a penny above the Street view of $0.19, as compiled by Capital IQ. Francesca's reported fiscal Q4 revenue of $138.5 million, down from $146.3 million, and exactly in line with Street views. In guidance, the company said it expected a fiscal Q1 loss per share of $0.10 to $0.13, on revenue of $100 million to $103 million. The Street view is for a profit of $0.14 per share, and revenue of $111.1 million. For fiscal year ending Feb, 2, 2019, the company said it expects EPS of $0.53 to $0.63, and revenue of $485 million to $499 million. The Street view is for EPS of $0.63 and revenue of $492.9 million.
Winners and Losers
Financial
The Select Financial Sector SPDRs ( XLF ) was flat. Direxion Daily Financial Bull 3X shares (FAS) and its bearish counterpart Direxion Daily Financial Bear 3X shares (FAZ) were inactive.
JLL Spark, a division of Jones Lang LaSalle (JLL), said that it set up a fund to invest up to $100 million in companies focused on leveraging technology to improve "everything from real-estate development and management to leasing and investing." The JLL Spark Global Venture fund will also help entrepreneurs and their companies by connecting them with JLL's business lines and clients for feedback and distribution of their products, according to a statement. The fund will focus on seed and Series A investments, as well as select late-stage rounds. Typical investment size will range from a few hundred thousand to several million dollars.
Technology
Technology Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLK) and other tech funds iShares Dow Jones US Technology ETF (IYW), iShares S&P North American Technology ETF (IGM) and iShares S&P North American Technology-Software Index (IGV) were inactive.
Among semiconductor ETFs, SPDR S&P Semiconductor (XSD) and Semiconductor Sector Index Fund (SOXX) were both flat.
Coupa Software (COUP) rose more than 3% after it reported non-GAAP net loss per share was $0.01 for the period ended April 30, compared to a loss of $0.09 per share for the year-ago period. Analysts had projected a net loss per share of $0.11, according to Capital IQ data. Fiscal Q1 revenue increased 37% to $56.4 million, from $41.1 million, surpassing the analyst consensus of $51.33 million. For fiscal Q2, the company anticipates non-GAAP net loss per share between $0.08 loss and $0.10 loss per share, and fiscal Q2 revenue between $56.0 and $57.0 million. Analysts had predicted a net loss per share of $0.11, and revenue of $55.6 million. For FY19, the company anticipates non-GAAP net loss per share to be between $0.14 loss and $0.19 loss per share, and revenue to be between $233.0 and $236.0 million. Analysts had forecast non-GAAP net loss per share of $0.24, and revenue of $230.1 million.
Energy
Dow Jones US Energy Fund (IYE) was flat and Energy Select Sector SPDR (XLE) was down 0.5%.
SandRidge Energy (SD) said it sent a letter to shareholders outlining what it said was activist investor Carl Icahn's poor track record in the energy industry, lack of a plan and false and misleading campaign against the company. Carl Icahn has submitted a rival slate of directors for election to the SandRidge Energy board at a June 19 annual shareholder meeting. Additionally, SandRidge Energy noted that proxy advisory firm, Glass, Lewis, has recommended shareholders vote for SandRidge's director nominees and withhold support on Icahn's non-independent nominees. Sandridge Energy reiterated its claim that Icahn wants control of the energy company without paying the normal market premium for that control.
Commodities
Crude was down 0.7%. United States Oil Fund (USO) was down 0.8%. Natural gas was down 0.5% while United States Natural Gas Fund (UNG) was down 0.1%.
Gold was down 0.2%. SPDR Gold Trust (GLD) was up 0.1%. Silver was down 0.2%, while iShares Silver Trust (SLV) was up 0.1%.
Health Care
Health Care SPDR (XLV) and other health care funds Vanguard Health Care ETF (VHT) and iShares Dow Jones US Healthcare (IYH) were flat. Biotechnology fund iShares NASDAQ Biotechnology Index (IBB) was inactive.
Eli Lilly (LLY) rose 1% after it said it secured US Food and Drug Administration approval for a new indication for Alimta in combination with carboplatin and Merck's (MRK) Keytruda for the initial treatment of patients with metastatic nonsquamous non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). This is the first and only combination of chemotherapy and immunotherapy to earn FDA approval for the first-line treatment of metastatic nonsquamous NSCLC, Eli Lilly said. This indication is approved based on tumor response rate and progression-free survival, the company said adding that continued approval for this indication may be contingent upon verification and description of clinical benefit in the confirmatory trials. Merck received accelerated approval for the combination of Keytruda with Alimta and carboplatin in May 2017.
